title: France – Construction work – MGP - Réhabilitation des locaux de service et des logements du Quartier Hoche à Wissembourg (67)
description: Le marché issu de la présente consultation est un marché global de performance (MGP), au sens de l’article L. 2171-3 du Code de la commande publique. Il porte sur la réhabilitation des locaux de service et des logements du quartier Hoche à Wissembourg (67) et associe des prestations de conception, de réalisation, d’exploitation-maintenance et de suivi des performances. Au stade de la candidature, une note synthétique présente le contexte, le périmètre, les enjeux, les principales contraintes et les caractéristiques de l’opération. Elle ne constitue ni le programme fonctionnel et performanciel définitif, ni le projet de marché. Ces documents, accompagnés des diagnostics, études disponibles et cadres de réponse, seront transmis aux seuls candidats admis à soumissionner. Le marché comporte des objectifs chiffrés et des engagements mesurables, notamment en matière de performance énergétique, de qualité d’usage, d’exploitation-maintenance et de suivi des consommations. Les modalités de mesure, de vérification et, le cas échéant, d’intéressement ou de pénalisation seront précisées en phase offre. Description sommaire de l’opération L’opération vise à réhabiliter les 158 logements et le bâtiment 23, regroupant les principales fonctions techniques de la caserne, afin de moderniser le patrimoine, d’améliorer les conditions d’hébergement et de travail, de fiabiliser les réseaux et équipements techniques et de réduire les consommations énergétiques. Le périmètre principal de l’opération comprend la remise à niveau technique et énergétique des 158 logements et du bâtiment 23, qui regroupe les principales fonctions techniques de la caserne, ainsi que la fiabilisation des réseaux, notamment de chauffage, d’eau chaude sanitaire, d’électricité et d’éclairage. Le programme intègre également des prestations d’amélioration du confort résidentiel portant notamment sur les pièces humides, les installations électriques et les parties communes. D’autres interventions sont également prévues, notamment pour répondre aux besoins de relocalisation de certaines unités opérationnelles et d’adaptation de bâtiments de service aux exigences réglementaires et fonctionnelles. Le périmètre exact des prestations intégrées à la base du marché et de celles faisant l’objet de variantes obligatoires sera précisé dans les documents de consultation remis aux candidats admis à présenter une offre. Les objectifs principaux sont de pérenniser le patrimoine immobilier, d’améliorer les conditions d’habitation des familles et les conditions de travail des personnels, de fiabiliser les réseaux et équipements techniques et d’atteindre une réduction des consommations énergétiques de 50 % sur les bâtiments de logements et le bâtiment 23, tout en garantissant la continuité d’exploitation d’une caserne occupée. Les prestations comprennent les études de diagnostic et de conception, les procédures et autorisations administratives, les études d’exécution, la réalisation des travaux, l’exploitation-maintenance ainsi que le suivi et la vérification des performances contractuelles.

title: Samfunnsøkonomisk analyse momskompensasjonsordningen for frivillige organisasjoner
description: Utreder skal gjennomføre en samfunnsøkonomisk analyse av alternative modeller for en eventuell regelstyring av merverdiavgiftskompensasjonsordningen (momskompensasjonsordningen) for frivillige organisasjoner i samsvar med Utredningsinstruksen og DFØs veileder i samfunnsøkonomiske analyser Analysen skal belyse nytte, kostnader og fordelingsvirkninger for staten, frivillige organisasjoner og samfunnet som helhet, samt vurdere konsekvenser for måloppnåelse, administrativ belastning, kontrollbehov og budsjettmessig risiko. Stortinget har fattet vedtak om regelstyring av momskompensasjonsordningen. Dagens ordning er forskriftsfestet med hjemmel i Stortingets årlige budsjettvedtak. For å oppfylle vedtaket om regelstyring må finansieringen legges om fra dagens rammestyrte bevilgning til en overslagsbevilgning. Bevilgningsreglementet som er vedtatt av Stortinget, fastslår at en overslagsbevilgning må ha hjemmel i regelverk fastsatt av Stortinget, jf. § 5 andre ledd nr. 1. Det innebærer at ordningen må forankres i lov. Regjeringen følger opp Stortingets vedtak ved å utrede grunnlaget for og konsekvensene av en eventuell lovfesting av ordningen. En regelstyring av momskompensasjonsordningen innebærer en grunnleggende endring av styringsmekanismen for ordningen. Ordninger med overslagsbevilgning er normalt basert på enkeltindividets rettigheter. Momskompensasjonsordningen derimot tar utgangspunkt i at organisasjonene årlig søker om kompensasjon, basert på totale driftskostnader med enkelte fradrag. Mer enn 90 prosent av mottakerne i ordningen får midler basert på en beregningsmodell, og ikke faktiske momskostnader (forenklet modell). I forenklet modell kan driftskostnadene inkludere lønn og andre kostnader uten merverdiavgift. Det betyr at i dagens ordning kan enkelte organisasjoner få mer i kompensasjon enn de har i faktiske momskostnader, mens andre kan få mindre i kompensasjon enn de har i momskostnader. Departementet vurderer derfor at det er nødvendig å utrede hvilke samfunnsøkonomiske virkninger ulike alterna

title: Skoleadministrativt system
description: Bakgrunn og formål Behovsbeskrivelse Harstad kommune skal anskaffe en ny skoleadministrativ løsning, som skal understøtte helhetlig forvaltning av grunnskole og SFO. Kommunen har utarbeidet en detaljert kravspesifikasjon som besvares av leverandør. Denne behovsbeskrivelsen skal derimot gi leverandørene en overordnet forståelse av hva som er særlig viktig for kommunen. Løsningen skal bidra til effektive, sammenhengende og framtidsrettede arbeidsprosesser på tvers av organisasjonen. Det er et sentralt mål å redusere manuelt arbeid, sikre god dataflyt og legge til rette for helhetlig styring og oppfølging av skolene og SFO. Løsningen må støtte administrative oppgaver i hele skoleløpet for elever, fra planlegging og daglig drift til avslutning og rapportering. Brukervennlighet og kvalitet i oppgaveløsningen er avgjørende. Løsningen skal være intuitiv og effektiv for alle brukergrupper, inkludert administrasjon, ansatte, elever og foresatte. Kommunen vil i evalueringen legge stor vekt på hvordan løsningen oppleves i praktisk bruk, blant annet gjennom leverandørs demonstrasjon av caser. Videre er det viktig at løsningen understøtter gode beslutningsprosesser gjennom tilgang til relevante og pålitelige data. Kommunen har behov for god rapportering, analyse og oversikt på ulike nivå, slik at både skole og skoleeier kan følge opp aktivitet, resultater og ressursbruk på en systematisk måte. Løsningen skal inngå som en integrert del av kommunens systemlandskap. Det stilles derfor krav til god samhandling med både nasjonale felleskomponenter og interne systemer, samt til at data kan gjenbrukes og deles på en sikker og effektiv måte. Sikkerhet, personvern og etterlevelse av regelverk er grunnleggende forutsetninger. Løsningen må sikre forsvarlig behandling av personopplysninger, god tilgangsstyring og etterlevelse av gjeldende lover og forskrifter, herunder krav til arkivering av bevaringsverdig informasjon. Harstad kommune legger også vekt på at løsningen er fleksibel og kan videreutvikles over tid. Det er behov for en plattform som kan tilpasses lokale behov og endringer i rammebetingelser, samtidig som den er robust, skalerbar og egnet for langsiktig forvaltning. Oppsummert etterspør Harstad kommune en løsning som: gir høy brukervennlighet og effektiv støtte i arbeidshverdagen gir godt beslutningsgrunnlag gjennom data og rapportering sikrer god samhandling og integrasjon med øvrige systemer ivaretar personvern, sikkerhet og lovpålagte krav legger til rette for videreutvikling og langsiktig forvaltning

title: Germany – Vehicle refuelling services – Planung, Errichtung und Betrieb von öffentlich zugänglicher Schnellladeinfrastruktur für E-Lkw auf bewirtschafteten Rastanlagen an den Bundesautobahnen in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland
description: Gegenstand dieses Vergabeverfahrens ist die Planung, die Errichtung und der Betrieb eines Schnellladenetzes für E-Lkw auf bewirtschafteten Rastanlagen entlang der Bundesautobahnen. Die Auftragsvergabe erfolgt durch die Autobahn GmbH des Bundes (in Vertretung für den Bund) im Rahmen einer Ausschreibung mit fünf Losen und betrifft die Planung, die Errichtung und den Betrieb einer verbindlichen Anzahl von MCS- und CCS- Ladepunkten auf insgesamt 227 Standorten. Jedem Los werden im Vergabeverfahren Standorte/Rastanlagen mit einer Anzahl an Ladepunkten zugeordnet. Es ist zudem möglich, dass die Anzahl der Ladepunkte auf einzelnen Rastanlagen während der Vertragslaufzeit steigt oder dass zusätzliche Rastanlagen hinzukommen; dies gilt insbesondere, wenn der Bedarf an Ladeinfrastruktur gegenüber der aktuellen Planung weiter steigen sollte und dieser Bedarf nicht durch den eigenwirtschaftlichen Aufbau ohne staatliche Förderung gedeckt wird. Für Ladepunkte zum Zwischenladen sind Nennladeleistungen von jeweils mindestens 400 kW (CCS-Ladepunkt) und 1 MW (MCS-Ladepunkt) vorgesehen. Die Ladeleistung kann durch die gemeinsame Nutzung von Leistungseinheiten mehrerer Ladepunkte sichergestellt werden. Für MCS-Ladepunkte muss in diesem Fall die an einem Ladepunkt vorgehaltene Leistung unter Berücksichtigung mehrerer zeitgleicher Ladevorgänge an denselben Leistungseinheiten zugeordneten Ladepunkten mindestens 800 kW (Mindestladeleistung) betragen; an CCS-Ladepunkten zum Übernachtladen beträgt dieser Wert mindestens 150 kW (Mindestladeleistung). Die Herstellung der dafür erforderlichen Netzanschlüsse beantragt die Autobahn GmbH des Bundes bei dem jeweils zuständigen Netzbetreiber.

title: NADSTAVBOVÉ ŘÍZENÍ SSZ V ČESKÝCH BUDĚJOVICÍCH – DOPRAVNĚ ZÁVISLÉ ŘÍZENÍ
description: Předmětem plnění veřejné zakázky je realizace softwarových úprav, zpracování související projektové dokumentace a implementace nadstavbového řízení dopravy pro celkem 41 řadičů světelných signalizačních zařízení (SSZ) v 6 vybraných lokalitách na území města České Budějovice. Hlavním cílem je povýšit stávající systém řízení na úrovni oblastí na dopravně závislé řízení, které bude v reálném čase flexibilně reagovat na aktuální dopravní poptávku, klimatické podmínky, nehody či uzavírky. Součástí zakázky je kompletní návrh řídicích algoritmů a změn signálních plánů, jakož i dodání dopravní simulace včetně ex-ante vyhodnocení kvality navrženého řešení v rámci definované architektury stávající dopravní řídicí ústředny (DŘÚ). Nové nadstavbové řízení bude implementováno s plným využitím stávající infrastruktury a licencí zadavatele. Algoritmy budou naprogramovány v běžném programovacím jazyku (Python, JavaScript, C#, Java apod.) s využitím přenášení strukturovaných dat prostřednictvím JSON v rámci stávající licence VAPW na DŘÚ VRS 5000 Web. Systém bude pro komunikaci a přenos potřebných DI dat z externích modulů a dat umísených na ústředně, což umožní efektivní integraci stávajících zdrojů dat a dalších telematických systémů města, jako jsou strategické detektory dopravy a systémy pro preferenci vozidel MHD a složek IZS. Výsledné řešení musí prioritně zajistit zvýšení plynulosti a bezpečnosti provozu na hlavních pozemních komunikacích, zrychlení průjezdu veřejné dopravy, podporu cyklistů a chodců a celkové snížení negativních externalit z dopravy (hluk, emise). Dopravní data ze strategických detektorů nebo z DIŘC využívají formát XML. Pro vyloučení všech pochybností zadavatel uvádí, že předmětem plnění jsou výhradně koncepční, projekční a softwarové práce včetně následného testování a odladění algoritmu nadstavbového řízení a systému s využitím stáváních licencí a architektury řešení. Předmětem plnění se předpokládá dodávka dle navrhovaného rámcového rozpočtu, který vychází z Technického popisu řešení a Popisu současného stavu. Jedná se zejména o tyto položky pro SSZ a nadstavbové řízení: - Dokumentace pro 6 oblastí a 41 SSZ; - SW pro řadiče včetně odladění; - Nastavení DŘÚ pro nadstavbové řízení (NŘ); - Dokumentace pro vlastní nastavení a popisu algoritmu NŘ pro každou oblast a křižovatku; - Zajištění všech instalací na HW a na síti SMČB včetně předání licencí, a zajištění NŘ a vlastní dodávky a instalace SW z pohledu kybernetické bezpečnosti; - Návrh a implementace NŘ v každé oblasti řízení města na SSZ; - Ověření a ladění NŘ v každé oblasti řízení města na SSZ; - Simulace algoritmu řízení a ověření jeho dopadu na dopravu pro každou oblast a SSZ; - Vazba na vstupní DI data, jež jsou k dispozici na DIŘC a ústředně VRS; - Vyhodnocení a ověření simulace a ověření jeho dopadu na dopravu pro každou oblast a SSZ; - Kontrola, vyhodnocení a ověření včetně koordinace a školení. - Předání veškeré dokumentace DŘ pro SSZ, nastavení algoritmu, popis algoritmu NŘ, SW pro NŘ, nastavení simulace a veškeré potřebné dokumentace včetně manuálu. Toto bude předáno pro NŘ, jednotlivé SSZ a ústřednu a servery města. - Součástí předání budou veškeré potřebné SW, licence, zdrojové kódy, popisy a nastavení včetně potřebných rozhraní. Toto bude předáno pro NŘ, jednotlivé SSZ a ústřednu a servery města. Součástí zakázky nejsou žádné hardwarové zásahy, výměny řadičů, dodávky či modernizace technologických zařízení křižovatek, ani žádné stavební úpravy či zásahy do fyzické infrastruktury pozemních komunikací. Vybraný dodavatel je povinen provádět implementaci a ladění algoritmů s maximálním ohledem na zachování plynulosti provozu a bere na vědomí, že případné krátkodobé nestability v dopravní síti během testování musí být minimalizovány a operativně korigovány. Nové algoritmy budou na řadičích aplikovány formou nových signálních plánů tak, že původní signální plány zůstanou k dispozici jako záloha. Navržené algoritmy musí: - nadále umožňovat i ruční řízení v lokalitách řadičů, - nadále umožňovat preferenci MHD v odpovídajícím smyslu (tam, kde je zavedena) nebo další specifické záměry stávajícího dopravního řešení, a to v rámci nově stanovených scénářů oblastního řízení. Postup při implementaci vytvořeného dopravního řešení: Dodavatel má povinnost nejprve provést dopravní simulaci návrhu nastavení algoritmu řízení NŘ se stávajícími daty dopravního provozu a předvést funkci NŘ v simulaci zadavateli. Zadavatel poskytne potřebnou součinnost v předání potřebných DI dat, topologie SSZ včetně popisu formátu, v jaké data budou předána (rozhraní). Následně má dodavatel jako součást realizační fáze díla povinnost doladit/upravit dopravní řešení na základě předvedené simulace a připomínek zadavatele, provést opětovné předvedení zadavateli a až následně spustit upravené dopravní řešení v reálném provozu. Během reálného provozu dopravního řešení v období 6 měsíců od spuštění má dodavatel jako součást realizační fáze díla povinnost 2× doladit/upravit dopravní řešení (ve lhůtě max. 30 dní od doručení požadavku zadavatele) na základě požadavku a připomínek zadavatele. Nabídka musí být naceněna tak, aby pro každý řadič SSZ obsahovala 1× optimalizaci algoritmu na základě předvedené simulace a 2× optimalizaci algoritmu na základě reálného provozu v období 6 měsíců od s...

title: NADSTAVBOVÉ ŘÍZENÍ SSZ V ČESKÝCH BUDĚJOVICÍCH – DOPRAVNĚ ZÁVISLÉ ŘÍZENÍ

title: Table Top Folder Inserters
description: Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) produces approximately 7 million mail pieces each fiscal year from its fifty-two (52) mailrooms across the country, a portion of which requires folding and inserting. Some of the CRA's current tabletop folder inserters are approaching end of life and require replacement. The CRA intends to award a contract to one Contractor for the supply, delivery, installation, training, maintenance, and ongoing support of tabletop folder inserters at various CRA locations across Canada. Firm Requirement • Supply, deliver, and install a total of five (5) tabletop folder inserters at the CRA locations identified in Annex A: Statement of Work. • Provide operator training for CRA personnel for each unit installed. • Provide one (1) year of on-site hardware maintenance and technical support for each unit. • Supply consumables and related accessories on an "as and when requested" basis during the contract period. The initial five units consist of: • Three (3) high-volume tabletop folder inserters; and • Two (2) medium-volume tabletop folder inserters. Optional Requirements At CRA's sole discretion, the resulting contract may include options to: • Purchase additional tabletop folder inserters during the first three (3) years of the contract, for delivery and installation at any location identified in Annex A-3. • Purchase additional on-site hardware maintenance for any unit purchased under the contract, for a maximum of five (5) optional years per unit. • Purchase consumables on an as-and-when-requested basis. The CRA currently operates thirteen (13) folder inserters across its network. This information is provided for industry awareness regarding the existing fleet size and potential replacement requirements. Actual quantities purchased during the resulting contract period, if any, will be determined by operational requirements and available funding. Proposal documents and supporting information must be submitted in either English or French. Bids must be submitted by using the Connect service provided by the Canada Post Corporation. When responding, the proposal MUST be delivered to: Canada Revenue Agency Bid Receiving Unit BRUg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids will not be accepted if emailed directly to this email address. This email address must be used to request that CRA open a Connect conversation, as detailed in Standard Instructions 2003. Bidders must not use their own licensing agreement for Connect to initiate a Connect conversation with CRA. The CRA reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. The Federal Contractors Program (FCP) for employment equity applies to this procurement. Bid Compliance and Remedy Process. The Bid Compliance and Remedy Process (BCRP) applies to this requirement. Refer to 4.2 – Bid Compliance and Remedy Process (BCRP) for more details. Communications - Solicitation Period Bidders are encouraged to submit all enquiries to the Contracting Authority as early as possible before the bid closing date. Questions must be directed in writing to the Contracting Authority via email Samuel.Snow@cra-arc.gc.ca

title: APN - Maintenance and Storage Hangar (Modified Design Build)
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE Maintenance and Storage Hangar Facility (Modified Design-Build) Ottawa, Ontario (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform design-builders of an upcoming contract opportunity in Ottawa, Ontario. The purpose of this APN is to allow design-builders to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested design-builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number: 87755 Approximate Estimate: $180M-$220M Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027 This project involves the design and construction of a purpose-built maintenance and storage hangar facility in the Ottawa region. The new building will provide modern, secure, and efficient infrastructure to support aircraft storage, inspection, maintenance, and operational readiness. The project will include the full design of the facility, site development, and construction of hangar bays, maintenance spaces, and associated support and operational areas. Additional scope may also be added through change order. The delivery method for this infrastructure will be a Modified Design-Build (MDB) contract. The estimated construction design and construction cost of this project is in the range of $180M–$220M (subject to further definition) whereas the additional potential scope is estimated at $120M (subject to analysis, definition and approvals). It is anticipated that this solicitation may be initiated in Winter 2027, conditional upon project approvals and funding authorization. The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In support of these commitments, DND aims to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through meaningful subcontracting, employment, and training related to the proposed project. To align with these objectives, the successful proponents will be required to develop an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) as part of the MDB contracts. The IBPs will outline proposed initiatives and opportunities for Indigenous participation, including subcontracting, employment, and training activities. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of Secret. 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing design-builders early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, design-builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, design-builders are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the design-builders to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a design-builders: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Design-Builders that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent  regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Priscille Vumi Leader, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada 343-596-6289 priscille.vumi@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the  proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) Data Center, National Capital Region
description: Advance Procurement Notice   Data Center, (Modify design Built) National Capital Region (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform design-builders of an upcoming contract opportunity located within the National Capital Region (Ontario). The purpose of this APN is to allow design-builders to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested design-builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Description of the Project and Services It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed Project Number: WA257004 Contract Number: 88262 Title: Data Center NCR Approximate Estimate: 1.5B to 1.85B Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027 Description: To increase its capacity in supporting the mid to long-term objectives related to operations, security, and technology modernization, the Government of Canada is planning to design and construction a data center facility within the National Capital Region. This Data center of 60 MW will enable the onboarding of next-generation capabilities with tailored mechanical and electrical configurations to meet distinct technology requirements throughout the facility. The proposed data centre facility will also include a small office space and a shipping and receiving area. The estimated cost of the proposed Modified Design-Build (MDB) Contract exceeds $1.5 to 1.85B. It is anticipated that this solicitation will be initiated in Winter 2027.  This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by the Government of Canada. Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. As of the date of posting of this Advance Procurement Notice, the required security clearance(s) are anticipated to be: for design-builders: a valid Facility Security Clearance (FSC).  Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing design-builders early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, design-builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, design-builders are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the design-builders to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a design-builders has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Design-Builder that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca   Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Stephanie Tanguay Regional service line leader, Contract services Defence Construction Canada 613-715-4626 stephanie.tanguay@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Local Guard Force - U.S. Mission United Arab Emirates (UAE)
description: The U.S. Department of State (DOS) has a requirement for a qualified Contractor to provide Local Guard Services to support the U.S. Mission United Arab Emirates (UAE) in Abu Dhabi and Dubai. The Government requires a secure environment to conduct their mission. The Contractor shall provide the organizational structure, management, and qualified staff at levels adequate to meet or exceed the requirement contained in the Performance Work Statement. The Contractor shall be required to provide services in a manner that prevent loss or injury to U.S. personnel, dependents, property; destruction of assets; to prevent unauthorized access; and deter potential terrorist attacks. Anticipated period of performance is for one base year and four one-year options (to be exercised at the sole discretion of the Government). See attached 19AQMM27R0019 for more details. Offerors are required to provide a signed Restricted Access Request (RAR) form to the POC prior to requesting access in sams.gov in order to view the solicitation and all correlating documents. The RAR and further details of obtaining access to secure solicitation documents can be found in History/Related Notice - PR15904172-Pre-solicitation. The Government will host a one time, optional site visit at the US Embassy at the time specified in Section L of the pdf document 19AQMM27R0019. Offerors who wish to participate must contact the POC of this solicitation and adhere to the requirements provided in Section L of the pdf document 19AQMM27R0019. Late requests will not be accepted and there will no make up dates. Offerors are NOT to contact the embassy directly. Offerors without confirmation of their pre-approval will be turned away on site. Vendors shall use the question format excel document provided and follow instructions as outline in Section L of 19AQMM27R0019. Questions over telephone or in person during the site visit are not acceptable. Amendment 0001 - correct a typo in Section L.9 - questions are due No later than Dec. 03, 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. All other terms remain unchanged.

R--Purdue Advanced Reactor Core Simulator Code
description: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing a presolicitation notice for a requirement entitled, �Technical Support for the Purdue Advanced Reactor Core Simulator (PARCS) Code Suite� The objective of this acquisition is to obtain regulatory technical support for the maintenance, code support, assessment, continued development, and user training of the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS code suite, including the interfaces between PARCS and RELAP, TRACE, and SNAP. These activities ensure that the PARCS code suite remains a reliable and modern tool for confirmatory reactor physics and systems analysis. PARCS supports independent regulatory decision making by enabling NRC staff to perform confirmatory evaluations of operator actions, core designs, power uprates, advanced reactor concepts, and license amendment requests. Maintaining and advancing the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS capability is essential for enabling high quality staff reviews under 10 CFR Parts 50 and 52. At a high level, this acquisition will: � Maintain and support the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS code suite, including version control, regression testing, documentation upkeep, bug identification, and corrective maintenance. � Develop and evaluate new code functionality, models, numerical methods, and interfaces needed to support emerging regulatory needs, advanced reactor designs, and new cross section methodologies. � Provide confirmatory analysis support, including model development, coupled system assessments, technical consultation, and code user guidance for NRC staff and program offices. � Deliver training and knowledge transfer activities to ensure NRC staff and authorized users can effectively apply PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS for regulatory analyses. The period of performance is five years with a 1-year base period and four 1-year optional periods. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the services required is 541990 �All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services.� Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 31310027R0003 will be posted on, or about, December 2, 2026, as full and open competition under FAR Part 15. Closing date for receipt of proposals will be on, or about, 30 days thereafter. RFP No. 31310027R00035 will be distributed solely through www.sam.gov. All future information about this acquisition, including solicitation amendments will also be distributed solely through www.SAM.gov . Interested parties are responsible for monitoring www.SAM.gov to assure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. The Government will not reimburse interested parties for any cost associated with responding to this business opportunity. Vendors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) database to receive a government contract award. Vendors must also be registered in Representations and Certifications Applications (included in SAM). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code applicable (541990 listed above) to this acquisition must be in vendor's SAM registration. Note: Update SAM profile to include all applicable NAICS Codes associated with your company. Vendors may register for SAM online at www.sam.gov or by calling 1-866-606-8220. In accordance with FAR 4.1102, offerors are required to be registered in SAM.GOV at the time an offer or quotation is submitted in order to comply with the annual representations and certifications requirements.

The U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Great American Outdoors Act (GAOA) Construction Team has a requirement for the following: The work will require placement of one multi-container living quarters structure, consisting of multiple storage containers, not to exceed 1,300 SF, according to Florida Building Code requirements, as well as the safety features attached in this document. The contractor will prepare site for new structure, install the structure and foundation, and establish connections to existing water, electricity, and septic tank service points. The contractor will build an access ramp and stairs to front entrance/exit and access ramp and stairs to secondary entrance/exit. This requirement is being procured in accordance with FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. This will be a Firm Fixed Priced Contract and Award will be based on Lowest Price Technically Acceptable. The complete Solicitation will be posted to https://sam.gov/ under Contract Opportunities on or about December 3, 2026. Interested contractors must be registered in SAM (System for Award Management, www.sam.gov) and complete Online Representations and Certifications. A pre-proposal site visit and instructions will also be announced with the solicitation. The NAICS code is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction and the size standard is $45 million. The project magnitude is between $250,000 and $500,000. The work will commence within 15 days of Notice to Proceed and be completed by the agreed upon date at the time of award. Bonding Requirements: 20% Bid Bond, 100% Payment Bond, 100% Performance Bond Direct questions in writing via email ONLY to Samantha LaGue at Samantha_LaGue@ios.doi.gov

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: SI-Assisted Omni Channel Experience - Request for Information
description: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) operates one of the largest contact center ecosystems in the federal government, serving people with Medicare, ACA Marketplace consumers, and caregivers across phone, chat, web, email, and mail channels. CMS is conducting market research to inform a potential future acquisition for SI-assisted omni channel experience capabilities. This updated RFI builds on an initial market research round (Notice ID 269999, February 2026), its scope is being expanded to include the ACA Marketplace, and incorporates findings from commercial payer benchmarking, vendor landscape analysis, and an internal Discovery Sprint process. This RFI is issued solely for market research and information purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, a commitment to issue a solicitation, or an obligation to award a contract. No proposals are being requested or accepted in response to this RFI. CMS will not pay for information provided in response to this RFI. This RFI serves three purposes: Validate and deepen vendor capability data. This RFI continues market research, building on information received from the previous RFI (Notice ID 269999, February 2026) and incorporating findings from commercial payer benchmarking and vendor landscape analysis. CMS is seeking evidence-based updates on vendor capabilities, pricing models, implementation approaches, governance and evaluation frameworks, and workforce transition approaches. CMS is particularly interested in responses that demonstrate sustained, production-validated performance, not launch-period projections. Surface evidence that resolves CMS's open Discovery Sprint questions, including the boundary between SI-assisted and human-required interactions, the evaluation and go/no-go criteria for scaling pilots to production, and the workforce transition and change management approaches required as containment increases. These questions are detailed in Section 5. Inform a defined downstream process. Vendor responses will directly feed the CMS Discovery Sprint, a structured four-week internal process, and the subsequent acquisition strategy. Responses will not be evaluated as proposals and do not obligate CMS to any acquisition path. Please see attached RFI document and Vendor Response Spreadsheet. Deadline: Responses must be submitted by January 5, 2027 at 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Submission Method: Vendors must submit responses by uploading their files to the designated CMS Box folder: https://cmsbox.app.box.com/f/2aa029c164ae47509a35879ffde9e2c3 Email submissions will not be accepted. Response Format � Questions: Vendors must submit their responses to the questions in Sections 2 through 6 using the RFI Vendor Response Spreadsheet provided with this RFI. Enter each response in the row and column assigned to that question. Do not retype questions into a narrative document in place of completing the spreadsheet. Supplemental Documents (Optional): Vendors may also upload supplemental documents to provide additional context, evidence, or supporting detail beyond what the spreadsheet captures. Supplemental documents are optional and limited to 40 pages combined, excluding organizational charts, and appendices containing production performance data. Supplemental Document Format: PDF or Microsoft Word. Font: Times New Roman or Arial, 11-point minimum. Margins: 1 inch minimum. Organization RFI Vendor Response Spreadsheet (completed, covering base question responses to Sections 2 through 6) Supplemental documents, if submitted, organized to mirror the section structure of this RFI, with each supplemental response clearly identifying the question number it addresses (e.g., TECH-1, SPRINT-5). For Section 5, respondents may answer all questions or select the subset most relevant to their proposed solution � please indicate which questions you are not answering and why. Appendices, if applicable: production performance data, system architecture diagrams, sample reports, and other supporting materials

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Zuni Comprehensive Community Health Center (ZCCHC) Cooling Tower Repair by Replacement
description: This is a PRESOLICITATION NOTICE for the upcoming Solicitation 75H70127R00002 Zuni Comprehensive Community Health Center (ZCCHC) Cooling Tower Repair by Replacement, located in Zuni, NM. These construction services will be in support of the Indian Health Service (IHS) prepared in accordance with FAR Part 36. The Government anticipates releasing the solicitation on or about December 01, 2026 and will remain open for approximately 30 calendar days. The solicitation and all amendments for this Request for Proposals will be posted on https://sam.gov under Contract Opportunities. A full scope of work, plans and specifications and Construction Wage Determination will be included in the solicitation documents. Additional details can be found in the solicitation when it is posted to https://sam.gov. SCOPE OF WORK: The purpose of this project is the removal and replacement of the existing cooling tower and cooling basin, along with all associated mechanical, electrical, structural, and control components necessary to deliver a complete, fully operational, and integrated condenser water system including all accessories, modifications, and incidental work for proper operation, safety and code compliance. The new installation shall meet or exceed current performance, reliability, and code requirements. LOCATION OF PROJECT: All work shall be performed at the Zuni Comprehensive Community Health Center, 12 B Ave., Zuni, New Mexico 87327. TERO: TERO fees do apply. (More information will be released in solicitation, but the TERO/Taxation & Revenue office phone number is 505-782-7111) CONSTRUCTION DURATION: Period of Performance is 240 calendar days from issuance of the Notice to Proceed. CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $250,000.00 and $500,000.00. SITE VISIT: Details regarding the Site Visit will be included in the solicitation. NOTE: ALL DATES ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGE. SEE SOLICITATION FOR OFFICIAL DATES, TIMES, AND LOCATIONS OF SITE VISITS AND DEADLINES. CONTRACT TYPE: The Indian Health Service intends to award a single Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract in support of this requirement. This solicitation will be procured as a Request for Proposal (RFP) in accordance with FAR Part 36 procedures with Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) evaluation criteria. This project will be solicited as 100% set aside for Small Businesses under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 238220 Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors. The associated size standard for this procurement is $19.0 million. For information concerning NAICS and SBA size standards, go to http://www.sba.gov. For the purposes of this procurement, a concern is considered a small business if its average annual revenue for the last five (5) years is less than $45.0 million. For information concerning NAICS and SBA size standards, go to http://www.sba.gov. Registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database is mandatory to be considered for award. Offerors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements via the internet at: https://sam.gov. Contractors are encouraged to complete SAM registration as soon as possible; the Government may not delay award for the purpose of allowing a contractor additional time to register in SAM. It is the responsibility of the contractor to check https://sam.gov frequently for any amendments or changes to the solicitation. Hard copy documents will NOT be available � all documents for proposal purposes will be posted at the website for download by interested parties. This notice is for informational purposes only and is NOT a request for submission of offers. No other information is available until issuance of the solicitation itself. No bidder list is maintained. Interested bidders should follow this solicitation notice on https://sam.gov to receive email notifications of any updates to the initial notice including any subsequent amendments. No additional information is available other than what is noted herein. Firms are instructed not to call requesting more information.

Background: Under the authority of Section 104 of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) or Super fund of 1980, as amended by the Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act (SARA); Subtitle I of the Resource Conservation and Recover y Act (RCRA) and pursuant to the National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan (NCP) (40 CFR Part 300); and in accordance with any reauthorizations or amendment s to any of the above named statutes and new response legislation, the EPA has been delegated the responsibility to undertake response actions with respect to the release or threat of release of hazardous substances, or pollutants and contaminants, that pose an actual or potential threat to human health or welfare, or to the environment. b. Navajo Area Uranium Mines (USEPA Region 9) The Navajo Nation encompasses more than 27,000 square miles, spread amongst the Four Corners Region of the USA (Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, and Arizona). The unique geology of the region makes the Navajo Nation rich in uranium, a radioactive ore in high demand after the development of atomic power and weapons at the close of World War II in the 1940s. Approximately four million tons of uranium ore were extracted during mining operations within the Navajo Nation from 1944 to 1986. Many Navajo people worked the mines, often living and raising families in close proximity to the mines and mills. Uranium mining and milling activities no longer occur on Navajo lands, but the legacy of these activities remains, including more than 500 abandoned uranium mine claims with thousands of mine features such as pits, trenches, holes, etc., and homes and drinking water sources with elevated levels of uranium, radium and other radionuclides. Uranium and other elements (selenium, arsenic, etc.) associated with mine and mill sites also occur naturally at elevated levels in rock, soil, surface water, and groundwater across the Navajo Nation and the broader Four Corners region. USEPA maintains a strong partnership with the Navajo Nation and, since 1994, the USEPA Superfund Program has provided technical assistance and funding to assess potentially contaminated sites and develop a response. In August 2007, the USEPA Superfund Program compiled a Comprehensive Database and Atlas of all known uranium mines on the Navajo Nation. In October 2007, at the request of the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, EPA, along with the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Indian Health Service (IHS) developed a coordinated https://www.epa.gov/navajo-nation-uranium-cleanup to address uranium contamination in consultation with Navajo Nation EPA. d. Region 9 The primary hazardous substance on all the sites referenced in the requirement�s Statement of Work (SOW) is radiological mine and mine related waste; therefore, a significant knowledge base of radiological material handling, environmental data interpretation, and data collection will be required to perform the activities within this SOW. The terrain to access site locations is rough, water is scarce, and the weather is often extreme in most areas. The trails and/or roads to the sites are not improved or maintained. To reach the site locations, 4-wheel drive vehicles (capable of drives over rough dirt/rocky roads) and/or hiking long distances is required. Roads can become impassable in wet weather, and conditions can change quickly. In summer, the conditions are hot and dry; in winter, elevations make them subject to severe cold and high winds. Due to the quick changes in the weather, be aware of the danger of flash floods. While this danger is greatest during the summer monsoon season (July through September), flash floods can occur at any time of the year. e. Purpose and Objectives: The purpose of the Navajo Area Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS) contract is to provide cleanup, response, and construction services to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), primarily at former uranium mining-related sites on or within the Navajo Nation (within EPA Region 9 in Arizona and New Mexico). 7.
